claim: Let \(B\) be the eight-vertex, twelve-tetrahedron ball of Benedetti--Lutz obtained from the Grünbaum--Sreedharan sphere \(S_{32}\) by deleting the seven tetrahedra listed in their Theorem 2. With the standard recursive definition of non-evasiveness, every one of the eight vertices is an admissible first vertex: for each vertex \(v\), both \(B-v\) and \(\operatorname{lk}_B(v)\) are non-evasive. In contrast, for pure vertex-decomposability exactly one vertex, the published label \(5\), is an admissible first shedding vertex. For every \(v\neq 5\), the deletion \(B-v\) is non-pure because it has maximal triangles as well as tetrahedra; deleting \(5\) leaves a pure three-dimensional complex and both its deletion and link branches are vertex-decomposable.

correctness.rationale: The exact published tetrahedron data reconstructs \(B\) with face vector \((8,25,30,12)\). The standard non-evasive recursion was replayed on all eight first deletion/link pairs and every pair passes. Under the pure vertex-decomposable definition, only deletion of vertex \(5\) remains pure; its deletion, link, shedding condition, and recursive vertex-decomposability all pass. The embedded verifier reproduces these checks from source data.

evidence: Benedetti--Lutz, Electronic Journal of Combinatorics 20(3), P31 (2013), Theorem 6.2: every vertex-decomposable ball is non-evasive.
General non-evasiveness results for convex or vertex-decomposable balls guarantee a successful root, not all roots.
broader_coverage.reasoning: The broader implication “vertex-decomposable \(\Rightarrow\) non-evasive” cannot determine the admissible-root set, and it cannot imply that the pure vertex-decomposable root set is the singleton \(\{5\}\).

value.rationale: The ball is the canonical vertex-minimal example that is collapsible but not extendably collapsible. The result identifies a mathematically natural separation on this extremal object: non-evasive vertex recursion is maximally flexible at the first step, while the stronger pure vertex-decomposable recursion is maximally rigid with a unique first vertex. This is structural information about the relation between two standard recursive simplification notions, not an arbitrary finite statistic.
